invoice_next_number.description: The number the next invoice gets.

default_invoice_notes.description: A note printed on invoices by default.

default_due_days.description: Days from the invoice date until payment is due, by default.

usage_close_delay_minutes.description: Extra minutes before a period's usage closes, for apps that buffer events. Usage closes about 6 minutes after the period ends plus this wait, never more than 30 minutes.

dunning_retry_days.description: Days after a failed charge on which to retry it.

create_pending_invoices.description: Whether new invoices are created in `pending` status.

auto_close_pending_after_days.description: Days after which a pending invoice closes by itself.

card_payment_limits.description: Card limit per currency, in minor units, keyed by ISO-4217 code. An invoice whose amount due is above the limit for its currency is not paid by card: automatic and manual collection charge only the customer's other payment methods, and the customer portal offers no Pay now for it. With no other method the attempt fails as `card_limit_exceeded` and the invoice stays open for the customer to pay another way. An absent currency or `null` means no limit.

credits_flexibility.description: Credits Flexibility — whether refundable credits and excess payments are AUTO-applied to an invoice, configured per credit kind and per invoice class. Every slot is optional: an absent one means auto-apply with no ceiling, which is the engine default and the behaviour of every business that has never set this. `null` resets the whole setting. Promotional credit is not covered (it is applied pre-tax and is already capped at the discounted subtotal).

dunning_config.description: Dunning settings for failed payments. Every member is optional — send only what you are changing; `null` resets the whole config to the engine default. Note that a partial patch REPLACES the stored config, so carry forward any member you are not changing.

mode.description: 'fixed' retries on your own day offsets and treats hardness as a single flag. 'smart' reads the gateway's decline code: transient refusals retry, refusals only the customer or you can clear hold the invoice open without retrying, and unrecoverable ones stop immediately. Default 'fixed'.

retries.description: Retry offsets. Offset N is counted from the Nth failure, not from the due date.

after_days.description: Days to wait before this retry.

final_action.description: Applied at the end of the dunning period (or on exhaustion when no period is set).

invoice.description: 'reverse' settles the invoice as paid via an adjustment credit note with reason code 'order_cancellation'.

subscription.description: What happens to the subscription. `cancel` (default) cancels it now. `cancel_at_term_end` cancels it at the end of the current term. `pause` pauses it now; you resume it by hand, and a subscription set to cancel at the end of its term is never paused. `stop_charging` keeps it and sets its `auto_collection` to `off`: later invoices are raised but never charged. `retain` keeps it and keeps billing. `cancel_at_term_end` and `pause` need an active subscription; any other status is cancelled now.

retries_by_method.description: A retry schedule per payment method kind, in the shape of `retries`. `card` covers cards, `bank_debit` covers ACH, SEPA, Bacs, BECS, PAD, e-mandate and NACH debits (1 to 5 retries; network caps and spacing still apply on top), `offline` sets the reminder days of auto-collection-off invoices. An absent kind uses `retries`. Other methods (UPI, wallets, PayPal) use `retries`. No retry runs while a debit is still pending.

adaptive_cadence.description: The timings `adaptive_timing` uses. An absent key keeps its default.

transient_hours.description: Hours after each failure for gateway and network faults. Default [4, 24, 72].

generic_days.description: Days after each failure for generic declines. Default [2, 3, 4]. With park_hard_declines, the invoice parks after the last one.

funds_gap_days.description: Days after each insufficient-funds failure. Null (default) retries on the next likely payday: the 1st, 15th or last day of the month.

plan_policies.description: Business-wide. A dunning policy per plan: plan id → `dpol_…`. An invoice runs its customer's policy first, then its subscription's plan policy, then the business settings. Each key must be a plan of this business and each value a live policy.

collect_on_payment_method_update.description: Charge open dues the moment a card is added. Default true.

require_successful_charge_on_reactivatio.description: Whether a reactivation whose charge FAILS is refused, leaving the subscription cancelled. Omitted, it inherits `collect_on_payment_method_update`, which is the field it was split out of — so a business configured before the split is unaffected.

skip_retries_for_hard_failures.description: A hard decline ends dunning immediately. Default true.

enabled.description: Master switch. False → a failed charge settles to not_paid with no automatic retries. Default true.

dunning_period_days.description: Days after the invoice due date at whose end the final action applies. Null (default) = no deadline; the retry schedule alone decides.

dun_trial_and_future_subscriptions.description: Dun failed activation charges on 'future' / 'in_trial' subscriptions. Default true.

dun_one_time_invoices.description: Dun invoices with no subscription behind them. Default false.

dun_offline_invoices.description: Dun auto-collect-off (send-invoice) invoices: the invoice is enrolled in dunning when it is raised (payment_due + dunning_status in_progress) and the customer is reminded on each retry offset. No charge is ever attempted, no attempt is counted, and the invoice stays payable in the portal throughout. With dunning_period_days set, the final action applies at the end of that period; without one the reminders continue and nothing is voided. Default true — send false to opt out.

no_payment_method_at_renewal.description: What a renewal does when the customer has no payment method at all (auto-collection on). follow_final_action (default) applies final_action.subscription; cancel cancels the subscription at the renewal date with reason no_card, even when the final action is retain. Card declines are unaffected.

adaptive_timing.description: Smart mode only. Times each retry by why the payment failed instead of using the retry offsets: gateway and network faults retry within hours (4h, 1 day, 3 days), insufficient funds retries on the next likely payday (the 1st, 15th or last day of the month, up to 4 times), and generic declines retry 2, 3 and 4 days apart, then the invoice parks (park_hard_declines on) or reaches the final action. Day-based retries land at 10:00 local to the card's issuing country when it is known (the business's timezone otherwise), and every retry stays within 30 days of the due date and inside dunning_period_days. Mandate debits (UPI, e-NACH, card mandates) and other decline codes keep the retry offsets. The timings are heuristics, not card-network requirements. Default false.

minimum_amounts.description: Minimum amount still owed, per currency, before dunning chases an invoice. Keys are upper-case currency codes, values are positive integers in minor units, for example {"USD": 500}. When an invoice's amount due (what is left after payments) is below the minimum for its currency, dunning does not start and dunning makes no retry or reminder for it. A currency with no entry has no minimum. Default {} (no minimum).

park_hard_declines.description: Smart mode, plus fixed mode's mandate and gateway-limit refusals. true parks a hard-recoverable decline (expired or invalid card, authentication required, mandate refusals, and a generic decline after 4 failed attempts): no automatic retries, reminder emails, then one last attempt and the final action at the end of the dunning period (30 days after it parks when none is set). false (default) retries those declines on the schedule like any other and applies the final action when it runs out; with no dunning_period_days, card declines keep a 30-day window. Lost, stolen and seized cards are held for a new card either way (smart mode); fraudulent charges and revoked authorisations end dunning at once. NPCI's per-rail caps shorten the retry schedule in both cases.

default_prorate_on_change.description: Whether subscription changes are prorated by default.

default_invoice_immediately.description: Whether charges are invoiced immediately by default.

inherit_subscription_po_number.description: Whether invoices inherit their subscription's po_number. New businesses default to true; every business that existed before this setting was introduced is false, so its printed documents did not change. An invoice's own po_number always wins.

default_cancel_option.description: When a cancellation takes effect by default.

default_credit_option_for_cancel.description: How the current term's charges are credited on cancellation by default.

default_unbilled_on_cancel.description: What happens to unbilled charges on cancellation by default.

default_ar_handling_on_cancel.description: Business default for POST …/cancel `account_receivables_handling` when the call omits it

default_refundable_credits_on_cancel.description: Business default for POST …/cancel `refundable_credits_handling` when the call omits it

unbilled_charges_config.description: Invoice-now vs retain-as-unbilled per lifecycle event. Absent keys resolve to the behaviour before this field existed, which is not uniform: on_change and on_one_time_charge inherit default_invoice_immediately (column default false, i.e. defer), the rest default to invoice_immediately. Cancel and resume are governed by default_unbilled_on_cancel and the resume call's own option, not here.

on_create.description: What happens to charges when a subscription is created.

on_change.description: What happens to charges when a subscription is changed.

on_one_time_charge.description: What happens to a one-time charge.

pause_config.description: Defaults the pause and resume operations fall back to when the call omits them; every default is the value that means "pass no argument". `locked` lists the keys a pause or resume request cannot override: the pause and resume operations return 400 when the request sets a locked key to a different value.

pause_option.description: When a pause starts by default.

unbilled_on_pause.description: What happens to unbilled charges when a subscription pauses.

dunning_on_pause.description: Whether dunning continues while a subscription is paused.

charges_on_resume.description: How a resume AFTER the paid term ended bills the new term that starts at the resume (an in-term resume charges nothing). `invoice_immediately` (the default) invoices and collects it; `add_to_unbilled_charges` parks the full recurring amount for the next invoice. `next_renewal` is deprecated: accepted as an alias of `add_to_unbilled_charges`, stored and returned as that.

unpaid_invoices_on_resume.description: What happens to unpaid invoices when a subscription resumes.

locked.description: The pause settings a pause or resume request cannot override. A request that sets one to a different value returns 400.

billing_rules_config.description: Billing rules. Keys left out keep their stored value; `null` resets every key. The business read returns the resolved value of every key. Each default is the behaviour before this field existed.

trial_end_action.description: What a trial does at its end when the plan price sets no `trial_end_action`. `activate` (default) converts and bills; `cancel` cancels with reason `trial_ended`; `pause` pauses the subscription without billing, and a resume starts and bills the first paid term. The price's own value wins.

specific_date_cancel_final_period.description: What a `specific_date` cancel bills for the term it ends. `full_period` keeps the term's invoice; `prorated` credits the time after the cancel date; `nothing` credits the whole term. A `credit_option_for_current_term_charges` on the call wins. Absent, it follows `default_credit_option_for_cancel`.

required_reasons.description: Actions the API refuses (400) without a reason: `cancel_subscription` needs `cancel_reason_code`, `void_invoice` needs `void_reason_code`, `create_credit_note` needs `reason_code`, and `refund` needs `reason` on a payment or credit note refund. Default all false.

cancel_subscription.description: Whether a cancel needs a reason code.

void_invoice.description: Whether an invoice void needs a reason.

create_credit_note.description: Whether a new credit note needs a reason code.

refund.description: Whether a refund needs a reason.

failed_change_charge.description: When the invoice a subscription change raises and collects at once fails. `start_dunning` (default) retries it on the dunning schedule; `next_renewal` holds the first retry until the current term ends, also when the gateway reports the failure later; a change that resets the term (for example monthly to yearly) starts dunning at once. The change stays in place either way.

upgrade_proration.description: How an upgrade bills the rest of the term for the items whose price or quantity changes. `prorated` (default) charges the new price and credits the old one for the time left; `none` changes the items and books no money for the current term (a change of billing period still charges the full new term). An item added or removed is always prorated. A `prorate` on the call wins. A longer billing period is an upgrade.

downgrade_proration.description: How a downgrade bills the rest of the term: `prorated` (default) or `none`, as for `upgrade_proration`. A shorter billing period is a downgrade.

upgrade_gate.description: `invoices_paid` refuses an upgrade (409, `invoices_unpaid`) while the customer has an unpaid invoice in this business. Applies to every plan change: the customer portal, a hosted checkout in change mode, the dashboard, the HubSpot app and the API (`…/change`, `…/schedule`, `…/items`, `DELETE …/items/{item}`, `…/update_for_items`), when the change is made or scheduled. Default `off`.

downgrade_gate.description: The same gate for a downgrade. Default `off`.

upgrade_timing.description: When an upgrade takes effect. `now` or `end_of_term` is the only timing every source accepts; `customer_chooses` lets the portal customer, or the API caller through `timing`, pick (omitted = now). Routes that can only apply now (`…/items`, `DELETE …/items/{item}`, `…/update_for_items`, a hosted checkout, the HubSpot app) refuse a change the rule sends to the term end. In a trial every change applies now. `null` (default) = not saved: the portal applies an upgrade now, and the dashboard and the API apply it now unless the caller schedules it.

downgrade_timing.description: When a downgrade takes effect, as for `upgrade_timing`; with `customer_chooses`, an omitted `timing` means the end of the term. `null` (default) = not saved: the portal applies a downgrade at the end of the term, and the dashboard and the API apply it now unless the caller schedules it.

new_customer_auto_collection.description: `auto_collection` for a customer created through `POST /customers` without one. Default `on`. Customers from the hosted checkout are always `on`.

partial_payment_write_off.description: The largest shortfall written off, per currency, when a recorded payment leaves an invoice almost paid. Keys are upper-case currency codes, values are integers in minor units from 1 to 100000, for example {"USD": 100}. The shortfall must also be at most `partial_payment_write_off_max_percent` of the invoice total. It is written off with an adjustment credit note and the invoice is paid. Credit purchase invoices are never written off. A currency with no entry writes off nothing. Default {} (off).

partial_payment_write_off_max_percent.description: The largest shortfall written off, as a percent of the invoice total. Both limits apply. Default 2.

declined_refund.description: When the gateway accepts a refund of an invoice payment and later declines or returns it. `block` (default for existing businesses) reverses the refund: the money stays with the business. `issue_credit` (default for new businesses) reopens the refund's credit note as refundable credit: it pays the customer's next invoices, and the next refund of that payment pays it out first. A refund the gateway refuses at once is not changed.

mandate_revoked.description: When a payment fails because the payer revoked the mandate (`revocation_of_authorization` or `debit_not_authorized`). `follow_dunning` (default) ends dunning and runs the dunning end action. `cancel_now`, `cancel_at_term_end` and `pause` end dunning and do that to the subscription; the invoice still gets the end action. `request_new_mandate` holds the invoice for a new payment method and emails the customer a payment method request. With any value other than `follow_dunning`, we never present a revoked mandate again (renewals and manual collection included) until a later success or a re-vault.

plan_change_term.description: Whether a change that moves the plan's price restarts the term (credits all unused time and charges the full new term from today). `keep_anchor` (default) keeps the term; `reset_on_upgrade` resets on an upgrade; `reset_on_any_change` on every plan change. A change of billing period always resets. `reset_term` on the call wins. Applies to `…/change`, `…/estimate`, `…/update_for_items`, the customer portal, a hosted checkout in change mode and the HubSpot app; a scheduled change keeps the term.

plan_change_coupons.description: What a change that moves the plan's price does with the subscription's coupons, before the change bills (manual discounts always stay). `keep` (default) keeps them; `drop` removes every coupon; `keep_if_valid` removes a coupon limited to specific plans that does not include the new plan. A business created in the dashboard starts on `keep_if_valid`. Estimates price the same result.

downgrade_credit.description: Where the credit a change gives goes. `credit_balance` (default) keeps it as account credit. `refund` refunds what is left of the change's credit note to the card or bank payments that funded the customer's invoices, one payment per refund (bank-debit money goes back to the bank debit). The refund can be partial: credit that no gateway payment backs (offline or credit-settled money), and anything left after a refund that is still in progress, stays on the account. `/change` returns `credit_refunds` with `refunded_minor` and `kept_minor`. `customer_chooses` lets the customer select in the portal (`credit_handling` on the portal change); other sources keep the credit.

reactivation_charges.description: How the reactivation of a cancelled subscription bills its new term when the request sends no `charges_handling`. `invoice_immediately` (default) invoices and collects it; `add_to_unbilled_charges` adds the full recurring amount to the next invoice.

payment_application.description: How payments meet open invoices. Keys left out keep their stored value. Each default is the behaviour before this field existed.

several_due_invoices.description: `separate` (default): one charge per invoice. `combined`: when the clock retries an invoice, the customer's other retries due now (same currency, same first card) are charged in one charge through a payment request with `origin: dunning`; each invoice keeps its own dunning attempt, schedule and end action. Not combined, so one charge each, when any instrument in the charge order is not a card, has a mandate, or needs a pre-debit notice, or when the total is above the card limit. `customer_chooses`: one charge each, and the portal may pay all open invoices in one charge (`POST /portal/v1/pay_invoices` without `invoices`).

invoice_order.description: The order a payment settles open invoices in: `collect_payment` and payment requests (the request keeps the order in `position`). `oldest_first` (default) = earliest due date (else creation) first; `newest_first` = the reverse. `customer_chooses` = oldest first, and the portal may pay a selection (`POST /portal/v1/pay_invoices` with `invoices`).

excess_payment.description: A gateway payment that settles for more than its invoice still owes. `credit` (default) keeps the rest as excess-payment credit. `refund` returns it at once (a bank-debit rail is still kept as credit; an offline payment is never refunded automatically). `customer_chooses` keeps it as credit, and the portal lists it (`GET /portal/v1/overpayments`) and refunds it on request. A duplicate payment for an invoice that is already paid is refunded whatever this says.

plan_credits.description: How plan credits that renew on their own clock behave around plan changes, the first window, pauses and a cancel at period end. Keys left out keep their stored value. Each default is the recommended option.

on_upgrade.description: The new plan's credits on an upgrade. `full` (default): at once, in full. `prorated`: at once, prorated for the rest of the window. `next_window`: from the next window.

on_downgrade.description: The new plan's credits on a downgrade. `next_window` (default): from the next window. `full`: at once, in full.

first_window.description: A first window that the subscription start cuts short. `full` (default): the full amount. `prorated`: prorated for the part of the window. `next_full_window`: nothing until the first full window. A price's `grants_credit.per_cycle.first_window` overrides it.

on_pause.description: Windows while a subscription is paused. `skip` (default): no grant for a window that starts while paused. `keep_granting`: grant as usual. `shift`: move the windows on by the time paused.

on_cancel_at_period_end.description: After a cancel at period end is requested. `grant_started_window` (default): grant each window that starts before the end. `stop_at_request`: grant nothing more after the request.

allowances.description: How allowances that renew on their own clock behave. Keys left out keep their stored value.

on_upgrade.description: An allowance on an upgrade. `new_window` (default): a new window starts at the change, with the full new allowance. `keep_used`: the used count carries over to the new allowance. `prorated`: the rest of the new allowance is prorated for the rest of the window.

invoice_rules_config.description: Invoice rules. Keys left out keep their stored value; `null` resets every key. The business read returns the resolved value of every key. Each default is the behaviour before this field existed.

small_invoice_action.description: What a renewal does with an auto-collected invoice whose amount due is above zero and below `small_invoice_thresholds` for its currency. `charge` (default) charges it; `write_off` writes it off as bad debt with an adjustment credit note.

small_invoice_thresholds.description: Per currency (ISO-4217 code), the amount due in minor units below which `write_off` applies. A PATCH replaces the whole map.

charge_timing.description: When we charge an auto-collected renewal invoice that has net terms. `at_creation` (default) charges it when it is created; `on_due_date` charges it on its due date. An invoice with no net terms is charged at once either way.

backdating_config.description: How far back a subscription or invoice may be dated. Absent resolves to fully permissive, which is the behaviour before this field existed; cutoff_day_of_month null means no restriction.

enabled.description: Whether backdating limits apply.

allowed_actions.description: The operations that accept a past-dated instant (`reactivate` is a checkout's `reactivate_from`). Absent resolves to all four; an explicit empty array permits none.

cutoff_day_of_month.description: The day of the month used as the backdating cutoff.

allow_past_invoice_date_on_create.description: Whether an invoice can be dated in the past when it is created.

allow_past_invoice_date_on_change.description: Whether an invoice can be dated in the past when a subscription changes.

reminder_config.description: When the reminder events (and their emails) are sent: per kind, a list of whole days before the date, 1 to 90, at most 5 different values (3 for `card_expiring`, `payment_due`, `pause` and `resume`). Each (record, kind, date, lead day) is sent once, with `lead_days` on the event. A kind you leave out keeps its list; null resets every kind to the default (`trial_ending` [3], `renewal` [5], `renewal_yearly` [30], `cancellation` [5], `card_expiring` "expiry_month", `payment_due` [], `pause` [], `resume` []). `[]` turns `payment_due`, `pause` or `resume` off. The business returns every kind, resolved. A lead day already passed when you change a list is not sent late. Mandate pre-debit notices are not configurable.

trial_ending.description: Days before a trial ends on which to send the trial ending reminder.

renewal.description: Days before a renewal on which to send the renewal reminder, for terms shorter than a year.

renewal_yearly.description: Days before a renewal on which to send the renewal reminder, for yearly or longer terms.

cancellation.description: Days before a scheduled cancellation on which to send the cancellation reminder.

card_expiring.description: `expiry_month` (default): `payment_source_expiring` mails the customer when the card enters its expiry month. A list of lead days instead sends `payment_source_expiry_reminder` (and the `card_expiring` email) on each day before the card expires. `payment_source_expiring` still fires once, without the email.

payment_due.description: Days before the due date of an open invoice that is not collected automatically: `invoice_payment_due_reminder`. [] (default) is off.

pause.description: Days before a scheduled pause: `subscription_pause_reminder`. [] (default) is off.

resume.description: Days before a scheduled resume: `subscription_resume_reminder`. [] (default) is off.

checkout_field_config.description: Which checkout fields show, hide, or are required. Absent keys resolve to defaults that are not uniform: billing.line1, billing.city, billing.state_code, billing.postal_code and billing.country are mandatory, everything else shows, and invoice.po_number is hidden (and still gated by storefront_config.collect_po_number). A mandatory region or postal code applies only where the country has one. billing.country cannot be hide (400). While the business has a live tax region, billing.country must stay mandatory, and while it has a GST region billing.state_code must too (400 otherwise; see `address_field_locks`). Making billing.postal_code mandatory is also the AVS/ZIP-verification control, since AVS is checked gateway-side.

customer.first_name.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's first name.

customer.last_name.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's last name.

customer.email.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's email.

customer.company.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's company.

billing.line1.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 1.

billing.line2.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 2.

billing.line3.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 3.

billing.city.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the city.

billing.state.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the state name.

billing.state_code.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the state code.

billing.postal_code.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the postal code.

billing.country.description: Whether checkout shows or requires the country.

invoice.po_number.description: Whether checkout shows, hides or requires a purchase order number.

shipping.address.description: Whether checkout collects a shipping address. hide (the default) collects none; show lets the buyer add one; mandatory requires one. The address goes into the customer's shipping address book as the default, and a new subscription ships to it. Tax still uses the billing address.

portal_field_config.description: Which billing-detail fields the buyer portal shows, hides, requires, or shows read-only. Absent keys resolve to defaults: customer.first_name, customer.phone, billing.line1, billing.city, billing.state_code, billing.postal_code and billing.country are mandatory, everything else shows. A portal save keeps the stored value of every hide or read_only key; billing.state and billing.state_code are one region, kept only when both are hide or read_only. billing.country cannot be hide (400). The tax rules of checkout_field_config apply here too.

customer.first_name.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's first name.

customer.last_name.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's last name.

customer.company.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's company.

billing.line1.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 1.

billing.line2.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 2.

billing.line3.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 3.

billing.city.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the city.

billing.state.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the state name.

billing.state_code.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the state code.

billing.postal_code.description: Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the postal code.

billing.country.description: Whether the portal shows, requires or locks the country.

chargeback_config.description: What a chargeback does to the invoice and the subscription. Absent keys resolve to record-only, which is the behaviour before this field existed. The invoice action applies to a LOST dispute only and its one value raises a DOCUMENTARY credit note (no ledger entries — the dispute's own dispute_losses posting remains the accounting treatment). A "mark invoice Not Paid" action is not offered: it would resurrect accounts_receivable with no matching ledger entry.

on_lost_invoice.description: What happens to the invoice when a dispute is lost.

on_initiated_subscription.description: What happens to the subscription when a dispute starts.

on_lost_subscription.description: What happens to the subscription when a dispute is lost.

cascade_to_other_subscriptions.description: Whether the subscription action also applies to the customer's other subscriptions.

stop_collecting_all.description: Whether to stop collecting on all the customer's invoices.

vies_validation_enabled.description: Validate customer VAT numbers against VIES. TRUE means validate — stated positively so the field reads correctly at its call sites. The switch exists because VIES is third-party and goes down.

storefront_config.description: What the checkout and self-serve portal do. Absent keys resolve to today's behaviour. The two URLs are the fallback for the checkout mint, which requires them per call when no default is set; a call with neither is still refused.

hide_zero_value_lines.description: Whether lines with a zero value are hidden.

collect_po_number.description: Whether checkout asks for a purchase order number.

default_return_url.description: The URL checkout returns to after a payment, when the request has none.

default_cancel_url.description: The URL checkout returns to after a cancel, when the request has none.

allow_invoice_download.description: May a buyer download an invoice PDF from the portal? Default true.

allow_invoice_payment.description: May a buyer pay an unpaid invoice from the portal? Default true. Turning it off removes the buyer's own payment path only — the engine still collects on its schedule and dunning still runs.

allow_remove_payment_method.description: May a buyer remove a stored payment method? Default true. Turn it off where a live mandate depends on the instrument.

allow_cancel_subscription.description: May a buyer cancel their own subscription from the portal? Default FALSE — the route is new, so granting it is the change.

allow_pause_resume.description: May a buyer pause AND resume their own subscription? Default false. One key for both directions — offering pause without resume would trap a buyer. Pause uses the business's own pause defaults.

allow_skip_renewal.description: May a buyer skip an upcoming renewal from the portal? Default false. Capped by `skip_renewal_limit`.

skip_renewal_limit.description: Most renewals a buyer may skip in 12 months. Default 3. Operators are not capped.

portal_show_usage.description: Show the buyer the usage so far on each metered subscription in the portal. Default true.

portal_show_usage_projection.description: Also show the projected usage at the end of the billing window. Default false.

allow_reactivate.description: May a buyer undo a pending cancellation? Default false. Covers a subscription still active with cancel_at_period_end; an already-cancelled one is refused, because restarting it bills a new period.

cancel_timing.description: When a buyer-initiated cancellation takes effect. Default `end_of_term`. The merchant's choice, not the buyer's — it is not accepted as a request parameter. Money handling comes from the business's own cancellation defaults, so a buyer cancel settles identically to an operator cancel.

portal_link_error_html.description: Rich text the customer portal shows when a buyer cannot get in — an expired, used, revoked or unknown link, or an ended session. Allowed markup: p, br, b, strong, i, em, u, h1, h2, ul, ol, li and a (http, https or mailto); anything else is stripped on read. Null keeps the default copy.

one_time_save_payment_method.description: Whether a one-time purchase keeps the buyer's payment method for later purchases. `ask` (the default) lets the buyer decide.

checkout_layout.description: Hosted checkout layout. `one_page` shows details and payment together; `steps` shows them one after another. Default `steps`; new businesses start with `one_page`.

wallets_first.description: Show Apple Pay and Google Pay above the form when the buyer's device and the payment gateway support them. Default false.

recurring_consent.description: The buyer must agree to the recurring charge (amount and period) before paying. Default false. The agreement is recorded.

require_terms.description: The buyer must accept the terms (and the privacy policy when set). Has no effect until terms_url is set. Default false.

terms_url.description: Terms of service link shown at checkout (http or https).

privacy_url.description: Privacy policy link shown at checkout (http or https).

marketing_consent.description: Offer an optional marketing opt-in at checkout. The answer is stored on the customer. Default false.

bot_check_after_failures.description: Ask for a bot check after this many failed payments from one IP address in 24 hours. Null (the default) turns it off.

allow_plan_changes.description: Customers can change plan, seats and add-ons in the portal. Which plans and add-ons they see is each product's enabled_in_portal. Default false.

seat_changes.description: Seat (per-unit plan quantity) changes in the portal. Default `off`.

allow_addon_changes.description: Customers can add or remove add-ons in the portal. Default false.

shorter_period.description: A move to a shorter billing period (yearly to monthly) in the portal. Default `always`.

charge_upgrade.description: When a portal upgrade is invoiced. `business_default` (the default) follows unbilled_charges_config.on_change.

change_statuses.description: Subscription statuses that may change in the portal. Default active and in_trial.

allow_cancel_scheduled_change.description: Customers can withdraw a plan change scheduled for the end of the term. Default true.

cancel_reason.description: Ask for a cancel reason in the portal (the business's cancel reason codes). Default `optional`.

retention_pause.description: Offer a pause before the customer cancels. Default false.

retention_pause_months.description: Length of the offered pause in months; null = no end date. Default 3.

retention_pause_choice.description: The customer picks 1 to retention_pause_months months. Default false.

parameters.description: Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key.

timezone.description: Modern IANA zone name for ORG-SCOPED display (the dashboard's system, audit and developer screens). Null or an empty string clears it, and null means UTC. Legacy spellings are rewritten to the modern one (`Asia/Calcutta` is stored as `Asia/Kolkata`); a fixed offset (`+05:30`) or a bare abbreviation (`IST`) is rejected with a 400. Not a billing input — subscription terms and proration key off the BUSINESS timezone.

icon_url.description: Square logo shown in the dashboard sidebar. An http(s) URL — upload one with `POST /v1/organization/brand_images`, or host it yourself. Null clears it.

409.description: Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload.

Bounded by construction, and explicit about the two different ways it can fall short of `total`: rows dropped by `split_limit`, and population the dimension does not describe at all. Read `kind` on each row rather than its `key` — a dimension whose own values include one called `other` makes the key alone ambiguous.

dimension.description: The dimension the measure was cut by.

returned.description: How many rows came back, residual rows included.

truncated.description: True when rows beyond `split_limit` were folded into the `kind: truncated` row.

exhaustive.description: True only when the returned rows' totals add back up to `total`. False means the rows are a view of the measure, not a decomposition of it — do not derive shares of the headline from them without reading `exhaustive_basis`.

exhaustive_basis.description: Why the rows do or do not add up. `rows_add_to_total` — they do. `row_totals_not_coincident` — each row's total is its own last figure and they do not all fall on the window's last period, so summing them is not the headline. `rate_not_decomposable` — a rate has no remainder, so no residual row exists. `distinct_count_not_additive` — distinct counts can share the same thing across rows, so they do not sum.

note.description: One sentence stating the same thing in words a screen can print.

series.description: The rows, biggest-first by magnitude with ties broken by key, with any residual rows last.

kind.description: What the row IS. `dimension` — a real value of the dimension. `truncated` — the rows beyond `split_limit`, added together; measured data, just not itemised. `unattributed` — the part of the population the dimension does not describe (a subscription with no plan, an invoice with no country), computed as the stored total minus every dimension row. It is a remainder, not a measurement, and it may be NEGATIVE for a measure with signed movement; it is never clamped to zero.

daily_digest.description: A summary at 08:00 business time of the day before: payments collected, payments that failed, invoices in dunning and cards that expire this month or next month.

enabled.description: Send this alert.

large_grants.description: An alert at the time someone gives free credit above `credit_config.grant_limits.<currency>.alert_above_minor`: a wallet top-up of type `granted`, promotional credit or a promotional credit grant.

enabled.description: Send this alert.

usage_close_delay_minutes.description: Extra minutes before a period's usage closes, for apps that buffer events. Usage closes about 6 minutes after the period ends plus this wait, never more than 30 minutes.

livemode.description: `live` for a live business, `test` for a test business.

live_business_id.description: On a test business: the id of its live mode. Null on a live business.

test_business_id.description: On a live business: the id of its test mode. Null until test mode is first opened for a business created before test modes existed — POST /v1/businesses/{biz}/test_mode creates it.

currencies.description: Currencies this business transacts in; null = unrestricted.

exchange_rates.description: The raw rate map: 1 default_currency = rate × key currency. Kept as numbers for the consumers that already read it; `currency_rates` below is the same rates with their provenance and is the one to prefer.

currency_rates.description: Per-currency rate + provenance (one row per configured currency, excluding the business's own default, which is 1 by definition). This is what a currency-settings screen needs: whether the rate is maintained by hand or refreshed from a provider, when the rate being held was PUBLISHED, and why the last refresh failed if it did.

week_start.description: First day of the reporting week. Default `sunday`.

fiscal_year_start_month.description: Month (1–12) the fiscal year starts in; default 1 (the calendar year). Fiscal years are named by the year they end in.

portal_field_config.description: The buyer portal's field matrix, resolved: every key present, tax-locked keys already mandatory.

created_at.description: When the business was created (ISO-8601 UTC).

AddressFieldLocks.description: Address keys the business's live tax setup forces to mandatory on checkout and portal. The settings refuse any other state for them.

country.description: The business has a live tax region.

state_code.description: The business has a live GST region.

CurrencyRate.description: One currency's exchange rate and where it came from. Reporting and the per-invoice snapshot only — no rate here ever decides what a customer is charged.

currency.description: The currency this rate is for (ISO-4217 code).

rate.description: Units of `currency` per 1 unit of the business's default currency, as a decimal STRING (exactness: see `Invoice.exchange_rate`). Null = no rate is configured for this currency, which is not 1 — a roll-up cannot convert it.

source.description: `manual` = maintained by an operator, and nothing will change it. `auto` = refreshed daily from `provider`. A currency configured before provenance existed reads as `manual`, which is what it is.

updated_at.description: When the rate being held was PUBLISHED by its source — not when we last checked. The ECB publishes on weekdays, so a rate fetched on Sunday legitimately carries Friday's date; reporting the fetch time here would describe our request rather than the rate. Null on an auto currency that has never refreshed successfully.

provider.description: Which source produced an auto rate; null for a manual one.

last_error.description: Why this currency's last refresh failed, or null. A failed refresh LEAVES THE PREVIOUS RATE STANDING (an absent rate would break the roll-up outright, a stale one is a visible inaccuracy), so without this the failure would be invisible: a rate frozen a week ago looks exactly like one that has not moved.

upload_enabled.description: false when this deployment has no object storage configured

accepts.description: The content types each asset accepts. `logo` and `signature` are narrower than the rest because they are embedded in the invoice PDF, which cannot carry GIF or WebP. Read this rather than hard-coding a file filter.

logo.description: The media types accepted for a logo.

icon.description: The media types accepted for an icon.

favicon.description: The media types accepted for a favicon.

signature.description: The media types accepted for a signature image.

product.description: The media types accepted for a product image.

asset.description: Which brand image this is. Decides nothing but where it is stored.

data.description: The image file, base64-encoded. Maximum 5 MB decoded.

content_type.description: Optional, and never trusted — the type is read from the file's bytes. Send it only so a mismatch appears in our logs.

url.description: The https URL to store on the business.

enabled_in_portal.description: Stored only: the customer portal does not read it yet, so it changes nothing.

plans.description: Plan product ids this add-on or charge is attached to. Replaces the whole link set — send the full list, not a delta. A charge needs a one-time price.

applies_to_all.description: Make this add-on applicable to EVERY plan (add-ons only). Omit to leave the flag unchanged; sending only `plans` never clears it.

applicability.description: Per-plan applicability level, keyed by plan id. Default `optional`. A charge is `mandatory` or `optional`, never `recommended`.

charge_on_event.description: The event that charges an attached item.

charge_once.description: True if the item is charged once instead of every period.

default_quantity.description: The quantity used when none is given.

billing_cycles.description: How many billing cycles the item is charged for.

min_quantity.description: The lowest quantity a customer can set in the portal. Null = 1.

max_quantity.description: The highest quantity a customer can set in the portal. Null = no limit.

quantity_step.description: Portal quantities go up from the minimum in this step. Default 1.

customer_can_change_quantity.description: False = the portal adds this add-on only at its default quantity. Default true. The limits apply in the portal only; your team can set any quantity.

config.description: Per-plan charge semantics, keyed by plan id. Defaults: subscription_creation, charge_once=false, quantity=1, no billing-cycle cap. A charge is always charge_once and never cycle-capped.

item.description: The attached add-on or charge product

applies_to_all.description: True if the addon can attach to every plan.

plans.description: The ids of the plans the addon can attach to (a slug id, e.g. `pro`).

applicability.description: How each plan treats the addon.

config.description: Per-plan settings for the addon, keyed by plan id.

grants_credit.description: Credit this price grants. `{"kind":"pack", …}` on a one-time price: each paid invoice line grants `amount` × quantity (paid credit, active once the invoice is paid). `{"kind":"per_cycle", …}` on a recurring price: `amount` × item quantity of promotional credit each period, with optional rollover. Null grants nothing.

unit.description: A credit unit id. Null = money.

amount.description: In the unit's smallest step (money: minor units).

expires_after.description: Packs: the credit expires this many days after the invoice is paid.

applicability.description: Which invoice lines the grant may pay: `{"kind":"metered"}` (every usage line, the default), `{"kind":"prices","prices":["…"]}`, or `{"kind":"meters","meters":["…"]}` (meter keys: the usage lines of every price that bills the meter when the grant draws). A `metered` grant takes the business's `credit_config.credit_scope` when one is set.

tax_treatment.description: Packs: required, or the business default. `taxed_at_use` is money only.

on_exhausted.description: What happens when the credit is used up, for a business with blocking on. Null = not set here.

rollover.description: Per cycle: `none`, or `carry` floor(remaining × percent ÷ 100) units (optionally capped) into a grant that expires `expire_after_cycles` periods later (null = never).

expire_after_cycles.description: Counted in reset windows when `reset` is set.

reset.description: Per cycle: when the credits renew (absent = each term). Each window gets its own grant, which pays only the usage inside that window. Credits do not renew by the hour.

first_window.description: Per cycle, a calendar window that starts before the subscription: grant it in full, prorated, or wait for the first full window. Null = the business setting.

meter.description: Bill from this meter's events. Models usage, tiered, volume or package. The usage aggregation is copied from the meter. Fixed after create.

unit_amount_decimal.description: The default rate: minor units per `quantity_divisor` units. A decimal string with at most 12 decimal places and no exponent, for example `"0.000125"`. "$3 per 1M tokens" is `"300"` with divisor 1000000.

quantity_divisor.description: The rate is per this many units. Default 1.

amount_source.description: `rate` (default): quantity × rate. `event_amount`: the sum of the events' `amount`. `event_cost`: the sum of `cost` × (1 + `markup_percent` ÷ 100). `model_price_list`: each combination at the selling rate: a fixed rate in `rates`, else its markup base × (1 + markup ÷ 100); a combination with no base bills `unit_amount_decimal`. `event_cost_or_list`: the events that carry a `cost` bill that cost × (1 + markup ÷ 100), on their own line; the events without one (or with a cost in another currency) bill as `model_price_list`; a fixed rate for a combination wins over both. The last two: the usage model only, on a sum or count meter with a `price_list` mapping.

markup_percent.description: `event_cost`, `model_price_list` and `event_cost_or_list` only: a decimal percent, 0 or more, up to 6 decimal places.

markup_base.description: `model_price_list` and `event_cost_or_list` only. `list` (default): the model price list, else your cost. `cost`: your cost, else the list.

rates.description: The rate card. A combination that no row names bills at the price's own rate.

id.description: Slug id for the price. Omit and it is derived from the name, or from currency/interval/model. Immutable once set; a collision is a 409.

external_name.description: The name customers see, when it differs from `name`.

trial_end_action.description: What happens when this price's trial ends.

billing_cycles.description: How many periods a subscription bills this price for; null bills until cancelled.

free_quantity.description: Units free in each billing period. They come off the quantity before the pricing model rates the remaining units. An item uses the value this price had when the item was attached, unless the item sets its own `free_quantity`. Flat and percentage prices do not use it.

portal_min_quantity.description: For a per-unit plan price: the fewest seats a customer can select in the portal. Null = the business's portal seat minimum. Your team can set any quantity.

portal_max_quantity.description: For a per-unit plan price: the most seats a customer can select in the portal. Null = the business's portal seat maximum.

type.description: Whether the price recurs or is charged once.

amount_minor.description: Required for flat/per_unit/package

interval_count.description: Number of intervals between charges, e.g. 3 with `interval` = month charges every 3 months.

usage_aggregation.description: Bill measured usage. Allowed on usage, percentage, graduated_percentage, tiered, volume, stairstep and package prices; refused on flat and per_unit. Fixed after create.

usage_recurring.description: Carry the measured level to the next period (seats, storage). Needs sum, last, max, unique or weighted_sum. A level that changes inside a period bills its peak (last bills the closing level). Fixed after create.

usage_time_unit.description: weighted_sum only (default hour): usage is billed in unit-hours or unit-days, the level times the time it was held, rounded half-up once per period. Fixed after create.

upToMinor.description: Inclusive upper bound. The tier starts after the previous tier's bound (the first at 0). Null on the last tier only.

rateBps.description: graduated_percentage only: the rate inside the tier, in basis points.

tiers.description: Required for tiered/volume/stairstep/graduated_percentage (stairstep uses each tier flatAmountMinor). Bounds must increase, and only the last tier, which must be unbounded, has a null upToMinor; otherwise 400. graduated_percentage tiers are over the money base in minor units: each takes rateBps of the part of the base inside it, plus flatAmountMinor once the base reaches it, rounded half-up once on the total.

package_size.description: Required for package: units per package

free_units.description: package/percentage: units (or base value) billed at 0 first

percentage_bps.description: Required for percentage: rate in basis points (250 = 2.5%)

minimum_amount_minor.description: Minimum spend for one billing period. When this price's line for a period is lower, period billing adds a true-up line for the difference, prorated on a partial period. Recurring prices only.

bill_usage_monthly.description: Recurring plan prices with a billing period of 2 months or more only. New subscriptions on this price invoice metered usage every month, while the plan fee stays on the billing period. Default false.

commitment_amount_minor.description: Recurring plan prices only. Minimum commitment for one full billing period. When the period ends, an invoice line bills the difference between it and the counted fees, prorated on a short period. New subscriptions copy it.

trial_period.description: Trial length, in `trial_period_unit`s. Omit for no trial.

show_description_in_invoices.description: Whether the price's description is printed on invoices.

show_description_in_quotes.description: Stored and round-tripped; no quote renderer exists yet to honour it.

tax_code.description: HSN/SAC for this price (India GST). The finest level of price → product → business default_tax_code; null asks the product.

tax_behavior.description: inclusive → the price already includes tax (backed out); exclusive → tax added on top

on_exhausted.description: What happens when the credit is used up, for a business with blocking on. Null = not set here.

id.description: Choose the customer's id instead of a generated `cus_…`. Unique within the business: an id already in use returns 409.

first_name.description: The ACCOUNT HOLDER. With last_name/company this is how a customer is named — there is no flat `name` field: sending one returns 400.

tax_exempt.description: Short-circuits tax to 0 with reason customer_exempt

email_notifications.description: false stops automatic billing emails to this customer. Emails an operator sends explicitly still go out. Default true.

dunning_excluded.description: true excludes this customer from dunning: a failed payment does not start dunning, and invoices already in dunning get no further retries or reminders. The first automatic payment attempt on a new invoice still runs. Time does not pass for dunning while the customer is excluded: setting false resumes dunning on those invoices, and every remaining retry, reminder and final action moves later by the length of the exclusion. Default false.

exclude_from_reporting.description: true leaves this customer out of every metric and report: MRR, churn, revenue, payments, analytics and exports. Use it for internal and test accounts. Billing is not affected. A change restates the stored figures in the background. Default false.

billing_cc_emails.description: Addresses copied (CC) on this customer's invoice, receipt and credit note emails, in addition to contacts with `send_billing_email`. Default empty.

billing_bcc_emails.description: Addresses blind-copied (BCC) on this customer's invoice, receipt and credit note emails. Default empty.

tax_behavior.description: Whether this customer's prices include tax. Set, it applies to every taxed line on the customer's invoices, whatever the price says. Default null: each price decides.

dunning_policy.description: The dunning policy (dpol_…) for this customer's invoices. Absent or null: the business dunning settings. dunning_excluded still applies first.

withholding_rate_bps.description: TDS: payer withholds this % of the net base (1000 = 10%)

custom_fields.description: Custom-field values; or pass top-level cf_<name> params

name.description: DERIVED, read-only (deprecated 2026-08-23): `first_name last_name`, else `company`, else null. There is no `customer.name` any more — sending this field to create or update returns 400. It is emitted only so a caller has a flat display string. Two distinct identities exist and neither is derived from the other: `first_name`/`last_name`/`company` are the ACCOUNT HOLDER (lists, emails, portal greeting), while `address.first_name`/`last_name`/`company` are the BILLING CONTACT, which is what gets printed on invoices and credit notes and sent to the gateway as the billing name.

currency.description: The currency the operator pinned on the customer, if any. Prefer effective_currency when deciding what to transact in.

effective_currency.description: DERIVED, read-only: the currency to transact in — `currency` when the operator set one, else the currency of the customer's live (active/in_trial) subscriptions, highest MRR winning a tie. Emitted by GET (detail) and by the list; absent from create/patch/archive responses. Null when there is nothing to derive from — fall back to the business default. Never write it back to `currency`.

lifetime_revenue.description: DERIVED, read-only: cash collected from this customer, one entry per currency — succeeded payments minus succeeded refunds. Credits applied to invoices are not cash and are excluded. Emitted by GET (detail) only.

currency.description: The currency of this entry (ISO-4217 code).

amount_minor.description: Cash collected in this currency, in minor units.

paid_invoices_count.description: Number of paid invoices in this currency.

first_paid_at.description: When the first invoice in this currency was paid (ISO-8601 UTC).

tax_exempt.description: True if the customer is exempt from tax.

email_notifications.description: Whether the customer gets billing emails.

marketing_opt_in.description: The customer's answer to the marketing opt-in at checkout. Null when they were never asked.

marketing_opt_in_at.description: The marketing opt in time (ISO-8601 UTC).

dunning_excluded.description: True if the customer is excluded from dunning.

exclude_from_reporting.description: True if the customer is left out of metrics and reports.

billing_cc_emails.description: Addresses copied on the customer's invoice and receipt emails.

billing_bcc_emails.description: Addresses blind-copied on the customer's invoice and receipt emails.

tax_behavior.description: Whether every taxed line for this customer is inclusive or exclusive. Null = each price decides.

withholding_rate_bps.description: The withholding rate on the customer's payments, in basis points (100 = 1%).

instrument.description: What the gateway knows about the instrument itself. Null when it reported none of it. A null FIELD inside means that one fact is unknown — in particular a null `issuer_country` is UNKNOWN, never 'not issued in India'.

funding.description: credit | debit | prepaid | … as the gateway spells it, lower-cased.

sub_type.description: consumer | business, verbatim — the gateways disagree on spelling.

issuer_country.description: Where the instrument was ISSUED (ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, upper case). Drives RBI e-mandate/AFA handling for Indian cards.

issuer_name.description: The issuing bank / PSP as the gateway names it.

fingerprint.description: Stable id for the same underlying instrument across customers and accounts. Stripe only; RazorPay and PayPal report no equivalent.

supports_international.description: A usage CAPABILITY (can this instrument transact internationally), not an origin — see issuer_country.

supports_recurring.description: Whether the instrument can be debited off-session at all. A mandate on one that cannot is a renewal that never collects.

three_d_secure_supported.description: True if the card supports 3-D Secure.

mandate.description: The mandate this instrument was registered under, as the PROVIDER reports it. Null on a plain card-on-file with no mandate rail. A null `max_amount_minor` means the provider reported no ceiling — unknown, NOT unlimited.

rail.description: Provider-native rail: card | upi | emandate | nach.

status.description: Provider-reported state; only `confirmed` can be debited off-session.

max_amount_minor.description: Ceiling the provider enforces per debit, minor units. A charge above it is refused before the gateway is called.

currency.description: The currency the mandate is for (ISO-4217 code).

reference.description: The mandate's reference at the gateway.

avs_check.description: What the gateway said about the address / CVC when this instrument was vaulted or charged. Null means nothing was captured — distinct from `unchecked`, which is a real verdict a gateway can send. Stripe only today.

line1.description: Result of the address line check.

postal_code.description: Result of the postal code check.

cvc.description: Result of the security code check.

clientSecret.description: For `mode: client_secret`: the secret the browser confirms with.

sdk.description: For `mode: sdk`: run this gateway's browser SDK with `params`. Post what the SDK returns as `client_result` with the completion request.
