shipping_address_id.description: Where this subscription ships: one of the customer's shipping addresses. Must not be archived. Omitted: the customer's default shipping address.

payment_method.description: One of the customer's saved payment methods (`pm_…`) to pin to the subscription. Collection charges it first, then the customer's backups. Must belong to this customer and not be `expired`/`invalid` (400). Omitted: the customer's primary.

id.description: Your own subscription id (letters, digits, _ and -). Auto-generated as sub_<nano> when omitted. Unique per business; a duplicate returns 400. Mainly for keeping ids when migrating from another billing system.

price.description: The price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`).

unit_price_minor.description: Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units; falls back to the catalog price when omitted

trial_days.description: 0 disables the plan's trial; omitted applies the plan price's trial_period.

trial_end.description: An exact trial end, in place of trial_days. Must be after the start; on a day-anchored business it names the day the trial ends on.

billing_anchor.description: Calendar billing anchor for the first period end

coupon_ids.description: Coupon codes applied at signup — discount the first invoice

discount.description: A manual discount applied at signup — a %/amount reduction with no catalog coupon behind it, discounting the FIRST invoice (a discount passed at signup lands on the first invoice, not the next renewal). Singular, because the engine allows one discount per subscription and refuses a second.

value.description: A whole percent 1-100 for `percent`; integer MINOR units for `amount`.

note.description: A note shown with the discount.

invoice_immediately.description: Signup invoicing. true (default) raises — and with auto-collection on, collects — the first invoice now. false queues the first period as a pending unbilled charge instead, so it rides on the next invoice and nothing is collected at signup (the response then carries `deferred_charge` instead of `latest_invoice`). Ignored for a trial or a future-dated start, neither of which invoices now. Distinct from create_pending_invoices, which governs RENEWAL invoicing.

create_pending_invoices.description: RENEWAL invoicing for this subscription: false posts an invoice each renewal, true opens a pending invoice that charges accumulate on until it is closed. Overrides the business default when supplied.

bill_usage_monthly.description: Invoice metered usage every month while the plan fee stays on the billing period. Needs a billing period of 2 months or more, in months or years, and no pending invoices. Default: the plan price's.

commitment_amount_minor.description: Minimum commitment for one full billing period; null for none. Default: the plan price's. Not with pending invoices.

custom_fields.description: Custom-field values; or pass top-level cf_<name> params

payment_intent.description: An intent (`pi_…`) the buyer authorized after this request answered 402 `requires_action`. The first invoice is settled by consuming it. Must belong to this customer, be `authorized` and match the first invoice's amount and currency.

client_result.description: What the gateway's browser SDK returned for a `next_action.mode: sdk` challenge, as string key/values. We send it to the gateway, which decides the outcome. A refusal answers 400 (402 on subscription create) with the gateway's reason, and the intent stays open for a retry. Rejected with `client_result_unsupported` on a gateway that takes no browser result.

on_charge_failure.description: What a declined first charge does, when the create charges now (auto-collection on, no trial, starts now, invoiced now). `refuse` (default): nothing is created and the call returns 402. `dun`: the subscription is created `active`, the first invoice stays open and dunning collects it, as after a failed renewal; the 201 response carries `payment_error` with the decline. `dun` with `on_session: true` or `payment_intent` is refused (400 `on_charge_failure_conflict`), because the buyer pays before the subscription exists.

current_period_end.description: The current billing term end. NULL while `in_trial` — a trial is not a term, so a trialling subscription reports `trial_end` instead and this is null (one or the other is reported, never both). Use `next_billing_at` for "when is this customer charged again?", which answers across every status.

next_billing_at.description: When the next invoice will be raised: trial end while in_trial, the scheduled start while future, the first renewal not skipped while active (or the next monthly usage invoice, when it is earlier); null once non_renewing/paused/cancelled, where no further invoice is due

bill_usage_monthly.description: Metered usage is invoiced every month inside the billing period.

current_sub_period_start.description: Monthly usage billing: usage before this instant is billed. Null when monthly usage billing is off.

current_sub_period_end.description: Monthly usage billing: when the next monthly usage invoice is raised. Null when off.

amount_minor.description: The amount in minor units (integer), e.g. 2900 = $29.00.

commitment.description: Minimum commitment for one full billing period, or null. See GET /subscriptions/{id}/commitment for the counted fees.

skipped_renewals.description: Upcoming renewals scheduled to be skipped, as the instants the clock renews at. See `skip_renewal`.

recurring_amount_minor.description: What one billing period charges for the recurring items, in minor units, net of discounts that last more than one period and before tax; null when cancelled or when an item recurs on a different cadence than the subscription

revenue_to_date_minor.description: DERIVED, read-only: cash collected on this subscription's invoices, in its currency — succeeded payments minus succeeded refunds. Credits applied to invoices are excluded. Emitted by GET (detail) only.

revenue_paid_invoices_count.description: How many of this subscription's invoices received a succeeded payment.

revenue_since.description: The first succeeded payment on this subscription; null when nothing was collected.

custom_fields.description: Stored custom-field values; also flattened onto the object as cf_<name>

shipping_address_id.description: The shipping address this subscription is set to ship to; null when it ships to the customer's default. Emitted by GET (detail), create, and an update that sends it.

shipping_address.description: Where this subscription ships now: its own address, else the customer's default, else null. Invoices record a copy when they are issued.

has_more.description: Whether more rows exist after this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque; pass as starting_after

next_offset.description: Present only while has_more; the same opaque token as next_cursor — pass as offset

label.description: A name for the address, such as `Home` or `Office`.

is_default.description: The customer's default shipping address. Mirrored as the customer's `shipping_address`.

archived_at.description: When the shipping address was archived (ISO-8601 UTC), or null.

created_at.description: When the shipping address was created (ISO-8601 UTC).

updated_at.description: When the shipping address was last changed (ISO-8601 UTC).

country.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code. Required to create.

is_default.description: true makes this the default (the previous default stops being one); false stops it being the default. The first address a customer gets is the default.

SubscriptionChange.description: ONE composition edit — item changes, adds and removes together. All three lists default to empty and at least one must be non-empty (an adds-only or removes-only call is legal). They are applied in a SINGLE transaction and every line they produce folds into ONE invoice, plus at most one credit note: one invoice is raised for one `update_for_items`, while splitting the same edit across `/change` + `POST …/items` + `DELETE …/items/:id` produced up to five documents — including an invoice that billed a full year of lines the next request removed, and a second invoice that on its own exceeded the payer’s per-debit mandate ceiling. Both `changes` and `adds`/`removes` are prorated from the start of the current billing day. The single-line routes still work unchanged for callers that add or remove one item on its own.

coupon_code.description: A coupon to apply AS PART OF this change. Applied inside the change's own transaction, BEFORE its proration invoice is raised — so the proration is discounted, which is the intended behaviour. Posting it as a separate call afterwards bills the proration at list price. `POST …/estimate` takes the same field and previews the same result.

coupon_ids.description: The same coupon as `coupon_code`, as a list. A subscription carries ONE discount at a time, so more than one entry is refused (400), as is a `coupon_code` naming a different coupon.

manual_discount.description: A manual discount to apply as part of this change — same shape `POST …/subscriptions/{sub}/manual_discount` takes, minus `note`, so one screen sends one body shape to the preview and the booking. `duration` defaults to `forever`.

value.description: 1–100 for `percent`; minor units for `amount`.

remove_discount.description: Remove the subscription's active discount (coupon or manual) as part of this change, inside its transaction and BEFORE the proration invoice is raised — so that invoice bills without it. With `coupon_code` or `manual_discount` it swaps the discount in one edit. On the estimate it prices the same order.

price.description: The new price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`).

unit_price_minor.description: Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units

adds.description: Items to ATTACH by this same call — priced exactly as `POST …/items` prices them, including plan-scoped differential resolution. A recurring add is prorated to the remaining term (the full term when this edit resets it); a one-time add is charged in full. Cadence is validated against the POST-change plan cycle, so an added yearly add-on is legal in the same call that moves the plan to its yearly price.

price.description: The price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`).

unit_price_minor.description: Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units

removes.description: Subscription item ids to DETACH by this same call — each credits the unused time exactly as `DELETE …/items/:id` does (a one-time item is credited nothing), into the same document as the rest of the edit. No line ever bills an item the same call removes. A mandatory add-on of the POST-change plan is refused; the same item may not appear in both `changes` and `removes`.

at.description: Backdate the change (proration as of this instant)

reset_term.description: Restart the term today and charge the FULL new-term price. Default false, and a SAME-CADENCE plan swap does NOT reset without it — a billing-frequency change always does, with or without it.

prorate.description: False suppresses the PRORATED credit and charge. On a term reset the full new-term charge is not a prorated artefact and still happens — only the unused-time credit is dropped, so there is no free term. Omitted = the business rule for the change's direction (`billing_rules_config.upgrade_proration` or `downgrade_proration`; unset, prorated). A value sent here applies to this change in either direction. A longer billing period is an upgrade and a shorter one a downgrade; on the same period the recurring amount per month decides.

timing.description: `now` applies the change; `end_of_term` schedules it for the current term end (the trial end in a trial) and returns `scheduled_change`. Omitted = the business rule for the change's direction (`billing_rules_config.upgrade_timing` or `downgrade_timing`); unset, `now`. Omitted with any of `at`, `reset_term`, `prorate`, `invoice_immediately`, `metadata` or a discount = `now` when the rule allows it. A timing the rule does not allow is refused (400). A change at the end of the term cannot carry those fields, or `on_charge_failure`, `coupons`, `downgrade_credit`, `plan_credits` or `allowances` (400 names them): it follows the business rules when it lands.

invoice_immediately.description: Invoicing options: true raises the proration invoice now and collects it; false queues the same lines as unbilled charges, folded into the next renewal invoice (where tax and account credits are applied). OMITTED resolves the business setting `default_invoice_immediately` (Settings > Billing LogIQ > Update subscription), which is off by default — so omitting this queues unbilled charges unless the business turned it on. Pass true explicitly to invoice now regardless of that setting. Credits (downgrade / term-reset) are issued immediately either way.

on_charge_failure.description: What a failed charge on this change's invoice does, for this call only. `start_dunning`: dunning retries it now, as any failed invoice. `next_renewal`: dunning waits for the term end (not after a term reset). Omitted: the business rule (`billing_rules_config.failed_change_charge`).

coupons.description: What this plan change does with the subscription's coupons, for this call only. `keep`: every coupon stays. `drop`: every coupon is removed before the change bills. `keep_if_valid`: a coupon that names plans and does not cover the new plan is removed. Manual discounts always stay. Omitted: the business rule (`billing_rules_config.plan_change_coupons`).

downgrade_credit.description: Where a credit from this change goes, for this call only. `credit_balance`: it stays as account credit. `refund`: it is refunded to the card or bank payments that funded the customer's invoices, as far as they can take it; the rest stays as credit, and the response carries `credit_refunds`. Omitted: the business rule (`billing_rules_config.downgrade_credit`; `customer_chooses` keeps the credit for a call made here).

plan_credits.description: How a plan that grants credits per cycle grants them at this change, for this call only. `full`: the new plan's credits for the current window now. `prorated`: the part of them that matches the rest of the window (upgrade only; 400 on a downgrade). `next_window`: the old grant runs to its window end, and the new plan grants from the next window. On an upgrade it replaces `billing_rules_config.plan_credits.on_upgrade`, on a downgrade `on_downgrade`. Omitted: the business rule.

allowances.description: How a raised meter allowance counts after this upgrade, for this call only. `new_window`: usage counts from the change. `keep_used`: usage before the change still counts. `prorated`: the limit is prorated over the window. Upgrade only: 400 on a downgrade. Omitted: the business rule (`billing_rules_config.allowances.on_upgrade`).

priced_at.description: `priced_at` from `POST …/estimate`. Send it only with `quote`, on a change applied now without `at` (else 400). The change is booked at this instant when it is at most 15 minutes old and no more than 5 seconds ahead of the server clock, so the unused-time credit is the one the estimate showed; otherwise it is priced at the moment of the call.

quote.description: `quote` from `POST …/estimate`. Only on a change applied now (`timing: now`, or omitted when the business rule resolves to now) without `at`; otherwise 400. The change is priced again with this body and refused (409, `param: quote`) when any amount differs from the estimate, or when the subscription renewed after `priced_at`. Nothing is booked. Omitted, no check is made.

CancelEstimateRequest.description: Mirrors the `POST …/cancel` body, minus the fields that record intent rather than move money (`cancel_reason`, `cancel_reason_code`). Every field is optional; omissions resolve from the business cancellation defaults, so `{}` previews the default cancellation.

cancel_option.description: `end_of_billing_term` ends at the close of the billed term, which is the current term — it is `end_of_term`.

cancel_at.description: Required when `cancel_option=specific_date`, and must be in the future. The estimate is priced AS OF this instant, because the scheduled-changes pass applies it as an immediate cancel with these same options.

include_cancellation_day_in_billing.description: Same as on `POST …/cancel`, with the same refusals.

credit_option_for_current_term_charges.description: How the current term's charges are credited: `none`, `prorate` or `full`.

unbilled_charges_option.description: What to do with unbilled charges: `invoice` or `delete`.

account_receivables_handling.description: What to do with unpaid invoices.

refundable_credits_handling.description: What to do with refundable credits.

at_period_end.description: Shorthand for `cancel_option=end_of_term`, honoured identically to the cancel route.

final_period.description: As on `POST …/cancel`, with the same refusals. Prices that credit. Omitted with `cancel_option=specific_date`: the business rule, as the cancel resolves it.

plan_credits.description: The business's plan credit rules, set for this call only.

on_cancel_at_period_end.description: As on `POST …/cancel`, with the same refusals. Moves no money, so the estimate does not change.

CancelEstimate.description: What a cancellation would cost, effect by effect. Amounts are minor units in `currency`. `net_collect_minor` is cash we would try to take, `net_refund_minor` cash we would send back, `net_credit_minor` non-cash credit granted — note that a refundable cancellation credit under `schedule_refund` appears in both `net_credit_minor` (granted) and `net_refund_minor` (leaves as cash), which `refundable_credits.includes_cancellation_credit_minor` quantifies.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts (ISO-4217 code).

options.description: The option set actually previewed, with business defaults filled in.

effective_at.description: When the cancellation takes effect. Every figure is computed as of this instant from TODAY’s state — for a deferred cancellation that state can still change first.

immediate.description: False when nothing moves today because the cancellation is deferred.

unbilled_charges.description: `action` is `none` when no option was set, in which case the pending charges are left stranded on the cancelled subscription (also raised in `warnings`). Under `invoice` the charges are taxed, customer credit is applied, and the invoice is raised OPEN — which is why it also appears in `open_invoices`.

cancellation_credit.description: `delivery` is `adjustment` when the term invoice is still open (it reduces what is owed), `split` when the term was paid (bucket-funded slices return to their buckets; only the cash-funded slice becomes a refundable credit note), or `none`. `already_credited` true means a prior cancellation credited this term and this one grants nothing further.

open_invoices.description: Invoices the AR step would act on, each with its due AFTER any adjustment credit. Includes the invoice `unbilled_charges_option=invoice` would create, marked `projected`. With `void`, an invoice that cannot be voided (a payment on it, one in progress, or tax withheld) carries `void_blocked` with the reason, is left open, and is not counted in `void_minor`. `mandate_shortfall` is set when the largest single collection attempt exceeds the instrument’s per-debit mandate ceiling.

refundable_credits.description: Refundable credit notes the CUSTOMER holds — not scoped to this subscription, because the cancel path is not either.

net_collect_minor.description: The net amount to collect, in minor units.

net_refund_minor.description: The net amount to refund, in minor units.

net_credit_minor.description: The net credit to the customer, in minor units.

warnings.description: Things that will NOT happen the way the option set implies. Empty means no known discrepancy.

SubscriptionEstimateRequest.description: The same request `SubscriptionChange` takes, minus the invoicing option (an estimate books nothing): all three lists, each defaulting to empty, at least one non-empty. Every figure it quotes is what `/change` then books for the same body — `changes` and `adds`/`removes` alike are prorated from the start of the current billing day, which is where each is actually booked.

coupon_code.description: A coupon to apply AS PART OF this change. Applied inside the change's own transaction, BEFORE its proration invoice is raised — so the proration is discounted, which is the intended behaviour. Posting it as a separate call afterwards bills the proration at list price. `POST …/estimate` takes the same field and previews the same result.

coupon_ids.description: The same coupon as `coupon_code`, as a list. A subscription carries ONE discount at a time, so more than one entry is refused (400), as is a `coupon_code` naming a different coupon.

manual_discount.description: A manual discount to apply as part of this change — same shape `POST …/subscriptions/{sub}/manual_discount` takes, minus `note`, so one screen sends one body shape to the preview and the booking. `duration` defaults to `forever`.

value.description: 1–100 for `percent`; minor units for `amount`.

remove_discount.description: Remove the subscription's active discount (coupon or manual) as part of this change, inside its transaction and BEFORE the proration invoice is raised — so that invoice bills without it. With `coupon_code` or `manual_discount` it swaps the discount in one edit. On the estimate it prices the same order.

price.description: The new price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`).

unit_price_minor.description: Custom price override (flat/per-unit only), minor units

adds.description: Items that would be added (`POST …/items`). A plan-scoped differential price is resolved exactly as the add would resolve it.

price.description: The price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`).

unit_price_minor.description: A unit price for this add, in minor units, in place of the price's own.

removes.description: Subscription item ids that would be removed (`DELETE …/items/:id`); each previews a prorated credit for unused time.

at.description: The time to estimate for (ISO-8601 UTC).

reset_term.description: True to estimate with a new term starting at `at`.

prorate.description: Mirrors SubscriptionChange's `prorate`, so a preview of an unprorated change quotes what that change will actually book. False suppresses the prorated credit and charge; on a term reset the full new-term charge survives and only the unused-time credit drops, so clearing it there RAISES the total rather than zeroing it.

coupons.description: As on `POST …/change`: the preview drops the same coupons. Not with a scheduled `change_option` (400).

downgrade_credit.description: As on `POST …/change`: decides `refunded_to_payment_method_minor` and `change_policy.credit_handling`. Not with a scheduled `change_option` (400).

change_option.description: `specific_date` previews the edit as `POST …/schedule` (type `change`) applies it at `changes_scheduled_at`, priced from today's state. A scheduled change carries only `changes`/`adds`/`removes`, so a coupon, manual discount, `prorate` or `reset_term` alongside it is refused (400). `end_of_term` previews it as a change scheduled for the current term end (the trial end in a trial) books it at that instant: nothing is left to prorate, and `next_renewal` is the renewal at the new composition. `prorate` and `reset_term` are refused (400); a coupon or manual discount is previewed onto that renewal.

changes_scheduled_at.description: Required with `change_option=specific_date`; must be in the future and inside the current term.

quantity.description: From -10^12 to 10^12. Negative only for a recurring sum or a weighted_sum price (a delta that lowers the level).

operation.description: `remove` takes `unique_key` off a unique metric (a seat leaves). Only for a unique price, and needs `unique_key`.

timestamp.description: When the usage happened (ISO-8601 UTC). Default: now. It must be in the period that the next invoice bills, and not more than 5 minutes in the future.

idempotency_key.description: Identifies this usage event on this item. It is the request key when there is no `Idempotency-Key` header. A reuse with different values is refused with 409.

note.description: Operator note, returned by the usage API and never printed on a customer document. Echoed in this response only when set.

subscription.description: Invoice only this subscription's unbilled charges (sub_…).

Invoice.description: An invoice. Money is integer minor units in `currency`. Since 2026-09-02 each invoice also carries the exchange rate that applied when it was finalized (`exchange_rate`), so a multi-currency book can be converted at issue-time rates instead of at whatever rate the reader holds today. It is **null on invoices raised before that date** and wherever no rate was configured — never assume 1.

dunning_status.description: Null when the invoice was never dunned. `succeeded` = the chase ended with the money in (renamed from `success`; the old spelling is never returned).

purpose.description: What an engine-made invoice is for: `usage_interim` = usage billed during the period when it reached the usage invoice threshold; `credit_purchase` = an automatic credit top-up. Null on every other invoice.

payment_in_flight.description: A debit has been accepted by the gateway and has not settled. **RETRIEVE only** — the list route does not compute it, so treat an absent key as unknown rather than as false. Collection is refused while one is live, so a UI must not offer "collect" against it.

awaiting_authentication.description: The in-flight debit is paused for the payer's own bank approval rather than for a settlement network — it is waiting on the CUSTOMER and expires unapproved. True when the gateway said so for this debit, or when the RBI/NPCI rule predicts it (INR over ₹15,000 on the card and UPI rails) for a rail that states nothing. NOT amount-gated: an issuer may demand additional-factor authentication at any figure. RETRIEVE only.

subtotal_minor.description: Line amounts LESS item-level discounts, before document-level discounts and tax. Reproduce it as Σ lines[].amount_minor − item_level_discount_minor.

total_minor.description: subtotal_minor − document_level_discount_minor + tax (± rounding). The promotional-credit slice is a PRE-TAX discount and is already netted out of this, so it never appears in `credits_applied_minor`.

promotional_discount_minor.description: The promotional-credit slice, applied BEFORE tax (it shrinks the taxable base) and reported as a discount with `entity_type = "promotional_credits"`. Included in `document_level_discount_minor`; already subtracted from `total_minor`.

item_level_discount_minor.description: Discount already INSIDE subtotal_minor (coupons scoped to specific item prices). Present on the single-invoice read only.

document_level_discount_minor.description: Discount applied TO subtotal_minor (invoice-amount coupons, plus `promotional_discount_minor`). Coupons also carry a discount line item; the promotional slice does not, because it has no coupon behind it. Present on the single-invoice read only.

discounts.description: Per-coupon discount breakdown, one entry per (coupon, stage). Present on the single-invoice read only.

scope.description: item_level is inside subtotal_minor; document_level is applied to it

entity_type.description: `promotional_credits` is the promotional-balance slice, which has no coupon behind it (`applied_coupon` is null).

source.description: What produced this discount. `label` cannot answer it: a manual discount is labelled "Discount" only because that is the engine's default invoice name, and a coupon may carry the same string.

coupon_code.description: The code the customer redeemed — a coupon SET's own code where the coupon was reached through one, otherwise the coupon's code. Null for a manual discount and for promotional credits. Kept apart from `label`, which is `invoice_name ?? code`.

line_item_ids.description: The lines this discount reduced ("applied on line item(s) #1"), as `lines[].id`. Empty for a discount applied to the invoice rather than to any line, such as promotional credits.

applied_coupon.description: The coupon code or id that gave the discount.

amount_minor.description: The discount amount in minor units.

credits_applied_minor.description: POST-tax customer-balance credit consumed at generation: the refundable + excess buckets. The promotional bucket is applied pre-tax and is reported as `promotional_discount_minor`, already inside `total_minor` — counting it here too would subtract it twice.

grant_credits_pre_tax_minor.description: Credit grants applied before tax (promotional, and paid credit taxed at purchase). Already off `total_minor`.

grant_credits_post_tax_minor.description: Money credit grants taxed at use, applied after tax. Included in `credits_applied_minor`.

amount_due_minor.description: Remaining collectible: total − withholding − credits − payments (0 when paid/written-off/voided)

withholding_minor.description: TDS withheld by the payer (reduces the collectible amount)

seller_state_code.description: SNAPSHOT of the seller's state at issue — what decided CGST+SGST vs IGST. Null on invoices raised before place-of-supply tax.

place_of_supply_code.description: SNAPSHOT of the customer's place of supply used for this invoice

tax_note.description: Reverse-charge / SEZ / export note to print. Null = nothing to print.

exchange_rate.description:
The rate that applied when this invoice was FINALIZED: units of the invoice's own `currency` per 1 unit of `exchange_rate_base` — the dialog convention (a `1 USD = 94.953741 INR` rate on an INR invoice with a USD base). A **string**, because the stored value is exact `numeric(20,10)` and a JSON number would round it to `94.95374099999999`; parse it with a decimal library, not `parseFloat`, if you are going to multiply money by it.

It is reported at the column's full scale, so that rate reads back as `"94.9537410000"` — trailing zeros are formatting, not precision. Compare rates numerically (or normalise) rather than by string equality.

Null = no rate was recorded — the invoice predates the field, or the business had no rate configured for this currency. **Null does not mean 1**: 1 would assert parity with the base currency. An invoice raised IN the base currency does report `1`, where that parity is a fact.

Frozen at finalize, so a `pending` draft carries null until it closes — a long-lived draft is stamped with its close-time rate, not its draft-time one. Reporting and audit only: nothing in the billing path reads it, and no rate here ever decided what the customer was charged.

exchange_rate_base.description: The currency `exchange_rate` is measured against (the business's default currency at issue). Stored per invoice so that changing the business default later cannot silently re-base history. Always present when `exchange_rate` is, and absent when it is not.

number.description: Human-readable sequential number; null while the invoice is still `pending` (numbers are assigned at posting) and on rows predating the column.

period_start.description: Service period start. Null on a one-off invoice with no period.

period_end.description: Service period end, INCLUSIVE — the business's anchor convention is applied before it is reported (`inclusivePeriodEnd`), so it is one unit BEFORE the stored exclusive boundary on a day-anchored business. The `invoice.generated` webhook carries the same value, so the two can be reconciled.

sub_period.description: A monthly usage invoice inside the billing period: the sub-period it opens (start, exclusive end). Null on every other invoice.

due_date.description: Net-D payment due date. Null when payable on receipt.

next_attempt_at.description: When dunning will retry. Null when no retry is scheduled.

paid_at.description: When the invoice was paid (ISO-8601 UTC), or null.

voided_at.description: When the invoice was voided (ISO-8601 UTC), or null.

void_reason_code.description: Why it was voided, as passed to the void route.

written_off.description: Written off as uncollectable; `amount_due_minor` is reported as 0.

po_number.description: The purchase order number printed on the invoice.

expected_payment_date.description: Collections FORECAST, not a payment term — nothing in the engine reads it, so it can never move a dunning date. Do not present it as a due date.

channel.description: Provenance at creation; null on rows predating the column.

billing_address.description: The address SNAPSHOT taken on this invoice if there is one, else the customer's CURRENT address — resolved here so every consumer (API, dashboard, PDF, portal) prints the same address for the same invoice. Null when neither exists. Unlike `customer.billing_address`, the contact name falls back to the account holder.

billing_address_is_snapshot.description: True = the address is frozen on this invoice; false = it is the customer's live address and will follow future edits.

customer_tax_id.description: The buyer's tax registration (GSTIN, else VAT id) as it stood when the invoice was issued. Null when none was on file then, or for invoices issued before it was recorded.

tax_origin.description: The seller registration printed on the invoice, frozen at issue. Null for invoices issued before it was recorded.

country.description: The country the seller's tax registration is in (ISO-3166 alpha-2 code).

price_type.description: Whether line prices included tax, at issue. Null when no tax region applied.

notes.description: The notes printed on the invoice, frozen at issue.

net_term_days.description: The payment terms that set `due_date`. Null when the date was set directly.

finalized_at.description: When the invoice stopped being a draft. A pending draft's `created_at` is its draft date.

updated_at.description: Last change to this invoice.

resource_version.description: Increases on every change to this invoice.

recurring.description: True when the invoice belongs to a subscription.

taxes.description: Tax per component and rate (e.g. CGST 9%, SGST 9%, IGST 18%). Detail read only.

rate_bps.description: The tax rate in basis points (100 = 1%).

amount_minor.description: The tax amount in minor units.

first_invoice.description: The first non-voided invoice of its subscription (or of its customer, when not recurring). Detail read only.

amount_adjusted_minor.description: Total of non-voided adjustment credit notes. Detail read only.

write_off_amount_minor.description: The part of `amount_adjusted_minor` written off. Detail read only.

total_minor.description: The credit note's total in minor units.

created_at.description: When the credit note was created (ISO-8601 UTC).

issued_credit_notes.description: Refundable credit notes raised against this invoice. Detail read only.

total_minor.description: The credit note's total in minor units.

created_at.description: When the credit note was created (ISO-8601 UTC).

applied_credits.description: Refundable credit from other notes applied to this invoice. Detail read only.

linked_payments.description: Every payment attempt, refund and reversal on this invoice, oldest first. Detail read only.

amount_minor.description: The transaction amount in minor units.

gateway.description: The gateway that processed the transaction.

id_at_gateway.description: The transaction's id at the gateway.

error_code.description: The gateway's error code, if the payment failed.

shipping_address.description: The shipping address printed on the invoice, or null.

shipping_address_is_snapshot.description: True if the shipping address is a copy taken when the invoice was created.

imported.description: Archival row imported from an external system (no ledger postings).

metadata.description: Key-value pairs you attach to the invoice.

created_at.description: When the invoice was created (ISO-8601 UTC).

customer.description: The payer (`cus_…`). Present on the LIST and the single-invoice read. The write and action receipts (create, collect, void, write-off, dunning, apply-credit) serialise the invoice alone and OMIT the key — an absent `customer` means unknown-in-this-response, NOT a customerless invoice. Never key a map on it unchecked: that is how a reader files every invoice under `""`.

customer_name.description: The customer's RESOLVED display name — `first_name last_name`, else `company`, else the legacy `name` column. Present on the list and the single-invoice read (same rule as `customer`). Null = the customer has no name of any kind; show `customer_email` instead. This is the ACCOUNT HOLDER, which is not necessarily the contact printed in `billing_address`.

customer_email.description: The customer's email at the time of the invoice.

subscription.description: The subscription this invoice bills (`sub_…`). Absent on a one-off invoice, and absent on the action receipts for the same reason as `customer`.

lines.description: The invoice's line items, in issue order. Present on the SINGLE-INVOICE READ only — the list omits them rather than paying the per-row query.

unit_amount_minor.description: The price of one unit in minor units.

quantity_decimal.description: The line's quantity, up to 12 decimal places. Read this, not `quantity`: a meter line carries its quantity here only.

unit_amount_decimal.description: The rate per unit in minor units, up to 12 decimal places. Read this, not `unit_amount_minor`.

cost_minor.description: A usage line's cost in its currency, fixed when it was rated. Only for callers with `usage_margin:view`; the customer never sees it.

cost_basis.description: `event`: the events' own cost. `price_list`: your cost, else the list, for events with no cost. `mixed`: both. `partial`: some quantity had no price. `none`: no cost at all. `no_rate`: an event cost in another currency had no exchange rate.

amount_minor.description: GROSS, before any discount.

discount_minor.description: Discount attributed to this line across BOTH waterfall stages.

item_level_discount_minor.description: The part of `discount_minor` that is already INSIDE `subtotal_minor`. Present only when the discount shares were loaded (the single-invoice read); the document-level part has its own row in the totals ladder, so showing it per line too would print the same money twice.

creditable_minor.description: The most a credit-note item that names this line (`invoice_line_item`) can still credit: the line's amount after discount, plus its tax when the tax was added to the price, less what non-voided credit notes already credit against the line. A tax line is worth its own amount. Never negative. Present on the single-invoice read only.

tax_code.description: SNAPSHOT of the HSN/SAC that classified this line at issue (India GST). Null outside that regime and on lines that classify no supply.

adjustment.description: A true-up line: `minimum_spend` (a price's minimum spend) or `commitment` (the minimum commitment). Null on every other line.

cumulative_minor.description: Threshold invoicing: the item's usage to date in the window, rated as a whole. `amount_minor` is this invoice's part. Null on other lines.

billed_before_minor.description: Threshold invoicing: what earlier interim invoices billed for this usage. Null on other lines.

rating.description: How a `usage` line was rated, written once with the line. Null on other lines. `tiers[].amount_minor` sums to the line amount; `level` is set for a recurring or weighted_sum metric.

price_source.description: Where a line's rate came from. `reported_cost`: an `event_cost_or_list` line of the events' own cost.

part.description: `event_cost_or_list` lines only: the events' own cost, or the events without one, billed from the list. Absent on a late line, which holds both.

segments.description: A `model_price_list` line: the rate and the rows it priced from. A price change splits a period into lines, one per segment.

base_unit_amount_decimal.description: The markup base's rate. Null on a `cost` base without `usage_margin:view`.

model_cost_override_id.description: Your cost row (mco_…). Only for callers with `usage_margin:view`.

unit_amount_minor.description: The unit amount in minor units (integer), e.g. 2900 = $29.00.

flat_amount_minor.description: The flat amount in minor units (integer), e.g. 2900 = $29.00.

amount_minor.description: The amount in minor units (integer), e.g. 2900 = $29.00.

price.description: The catalog price this line came from (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`), if any.

period_start.description: The start of the period the line covers (ISO-8601 UTC).

period_end.description: Inclusive, on the same convention as the invoice's.

state_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code, without the country prefix.

has_more.description: Whether more rows exist after this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque; pass as starting_after

next_offset.description: Present only while has_more; the same opaque token as next_cursor — pass as offset

amount_minor.description: The amount to add, in minor units.

item_kind.description: The kind of item the coupon applies to.

constraint_type.description: all = every product of that kind; specific = product_ids only

price_ids.description: Price ids of this item kind, for constraint_type='specific'. A line matches on its product OR its price.

code.description: The coupon's code. Letters, digits, underscores and hyphens only. Codes imported before this rule still apply.

kind.description: Whether the coupon takes off a percentage or a fixed amount.

amount_off_minor.description: The fixed amount off, in minor units, for a fixed-amount coupon.

duration_in_periods.description: The number of periods the discount lasts, for `repeating`.

max_redemptions.description: The most times the coupon can be redeemed.

max_redemptions_per_customer.description: Redemptions allowed per customer across their subscriptions; null = no cap. Applying past it is a 400.

redeem_by.description: The last time the coupon can be redeemed (ISO-8601 UTC).

valid_from.description: When the coupon becomes valid (ISO-8601 UTC).

invoice_name.description: The name printed on invoices for this discount.

apply_on.description: invoice_amount discounts the whole invoice; each_specified_item discounts only the lines matching item_constraints

item_constraints.description: Limits the coupon to certain kinds of item.

metadata.description: Key-value pairs you attach to the coupon.

meter.description: Meter features only: the meter whose usage this period counts against the limit. Null = the check compares `required` with the limit only.

key.description: lowercase a-z, 0-9, _ — the stable machine key your app checks

unit.description: The unit the feature is counted in.

meter.description: Meter features only: the meter whose usage this period counts against the limit. Null = the check compares `required` with the limit only.

key.description: The feature's key, unique within the business.

unit.description: The unit the feature is counted in.

value.description: "true"/"false" (switch), an integer, or "unlimited" (quota/meter)

same_as_credits.description: Always true: renew with the plan credits. Send it alone.

oneOf.description: When the credits or the allowance renew. `every`: hour (allowances only), day, week, month, quarter, half_year, year, `term` (once each billing term, the default) or `never` (once, kept until used). `count`: every N units (default 1; not with term or never). `anchor`: `subscription` (windows start at the term start, the last one cut at the term end) or `calendar` (on the hour, midnight, Monday, the 1st of the month, quarter, half year or year, in the business time zone). A window may not be longer than the billing term.

Renew with the plan credits. Each subscription follows the per-cycle credits of its own price of the plan (an active price first). With no credits reset, the allowance renews each billing term. A plan accepts the link only when its active prices grant credits each period on one schedule; a price change that splits that schedule is refused.

same_as_credits.description: Always true: renew with the plan credits.

reset.description: Meter features: when the allowance resets (every interval, the hour included), or `{"same_as_credits": true}` to renew with the plan credits. Null = the next invoice's usage window. Omitted = keep the stored reset. On a subscription, null uses the plan's reset.

code.description: Same value as `id` — the code IS the id

kind.description: Whether the coupon takes off a percentage or a fixed amount.

percent_off_bps.description: The percentage off in basis points (100 = 1%), for a percentage coupon.

amount_off_minor.description: The fixed amount off, in minor units, for a fixed-amount coupon.

oneOf.description: When the credits or the allowance renew. `every`: hour (allowances only), day, week, month, quarter, half_year, year, `term` (once each billing term, the default) or `never` (once, kept until used). `count`: every N units (default 1; not with term or never). `anchor`: `subscription` (windows start at the term start, the last one cut at the term end) or `calendar` (on the hour, midnight, Monday, the 1st of the month, quarter, half year or year, in the business time zone). A window may not be longer than the billing term.

Renew with the plan credits. Each subscription follows the per-cycle credits of its own price of the plan (an active price first). With no credits reset, the allowance renews each billing term. A plan accepts the link only when its active prices grant credits each period on one schedule; a price change that splits that schedule is refused.
